A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MLE-bench and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched across relocation and repagination, including the new Appendix A.9 in v6.

before.justification: v3 reports original agent evaluations on 75 competitions, scaffold and model comparisons, resource-scaling experiments, and contamination analyses in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains those original empirical results and adds analyses of performance by competition complexity, task category, and competition date in Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: The benchmark grading and submission rules, agent prompt, and documented AIDE, OpenHands, and MLAB modifications remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 and Table 7 retain the same scaffold components and hyperparameters.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 75 benchmark competitions, seven development competitions, and obfuscated-description scenario. Table 8 retains the competition inventory. The new category and complexity breakdowns analyze existing coverage rather than introducing datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same human-leaderboard reference and model/scaffold comparisons: four models with AIDE and GPT-4o with MLAB and OpenHands. ML-Bench is newly discussed as related work but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the stated preference for preserving original train/test ratios with a default 10% holdout and exceptions. Table 8 already specified that default in v3 and remains unchanged, indicating a correction to the reported protocol without establishing changed splits or rerun experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.9 substantially expands the analysis of performance heterogeneity: Tables 9–10 stratify results by complexity and task category, and Figure 9 examines performance against competition date. These questions were not analyzed in v3. The existing resource-scaling, contamination, and plagiarism analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds by default, with 16 for o1-preview/AIDE, 36 for GPT-4o/AIDE, and 10 for obfuscated descriptions, alongside mean and standard-error reporting. The added tables extend the existing uncertainty-reporting format without documenting new statistical procedures or increased runs.

E6.justification: The original results remain, including Table 2's 16.9% medal rate for o1-preview/AIDE. v6 adds a substantial performance profile: Table 9 reports its low/medium/high-complexity rates as 34.3/8.8/10.0%, Table 10 supplies category-specific outcomes, and Figure 9 shows weak performance after 2022. Some added overall rates conflict with unchanged Table 2, including GPT-4o/MLAB at 1.3% versus 0.8%; these are unexplained discrepancies, not established performance gains.

T1.justification: The pass@k estimator, familiarity definition, and mathematical content of the competition-description example are retained. No theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, 75-competition scope, leading 16.9% result, resource-scaling claims, and contamination findings. The added analyses support a more detailed assessment without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Figure 9 introduces the qualification that recent competitions are often more challenging when discussing weaker post-2022 performance. Section 5 removes the explicit caveat that the comparison with Weco's dataset difficulty cannot be confirmed because that dataset is unavailable. Section 6's limitations remain; the AGI-preparedness discussion moves into the ethics statement.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement changes code availability from forthcoming to publicly available, aligning it with the repository link already present in v3's abstract. v6 also expands the self-contained-description curation criterion and recommends the Low-complexity subset for resource-constrained use. Hardware, prompts, and implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Tang et al.'s ML-Bench and distinguishes repository-level code use from MLE-bench's open-ended solution development. It also shortens the SWE-bench and Weco AIDE discussions, including removal of the qualification about verifying Weco's dataset difficulty. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify curation and availability statements, shorten related work, and introduce Appendix A.9. The former AGI-preparedness section is incorporated into the ethics statement, and conference-header and author-footnote text changes. Most prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v6 adds two performance-breakdown tables and a competition-date scatterplot. Existing displays are retained with some relocation and reflow, including Figure 7 and Table 7. The principal figure designs and table organization are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly improves interpretability through the complexity, category, and date analyses, while making the split and code-availability descriptions more consistent. The original evidence and conclusions remain intact. These gains are limited by unexplained discrepancies between Tables 9 and 2, such as GPT-4o/MLAB's 1.3% versus 0.8% medal rates, and the removal of the caveat about verifying Weco's dataset difficulty.
